findings.checklist_item: Enumerate all reconcile_verdict consumers (gate_ops.completion_precheck, completion_sidecar) and specify how the new 'indeterminate' outcome is represented and handled on each verdict-producing/signing path, not just close_precheck.
evidence: reconcile_verdict called at src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:297 and src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:323 (in addition to completion.py:513) — none named in the plan
Plan step 2 names only 'reconcile_verdict' and 'close_precheck' as touch points
gate_ops.py:298-305 stamps `certifiable` onto the verdict and the close signs a verified-at-sha attestation — a new verdict value flows into the signing/certification path unaddressed
findings.finding: Step 2 changes reconcile_verdict's output (a new 'indeterminate/no-verdict-obtainable' outcome for non-PASS + zero findings + zero criteria), but reconcile_verdict has consumers outside completion.py that the plan does not enumerate: the workflow close-gate path gate_ops.completion_precheck (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:297) and the sidecar completion_sidecar.py:323. The close path the plan describes runs through gate_ops (which also stamps `certifiable` and feeds the signed close attestation), not directly through close_precheck's reconcile call.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; Acceptance Criteria bullet 5
scenarios: A close via the workflow gate (gate_ops.completion_precheck) hits the empty-findings non-PASS case, but only close_precheck's mapping was updated, so the workflow path still emits a bare FAIL
completion_sidecar reconciles a verdict into the new indeterminate state that downstream sidecar consumers do not recognize
findings.suggested_fix: Add gate_ops.completion_precheck (gate_ops.py:297) and completion_sidecar.py:323 to the plan's touch points; specify the indeterminate verdict's representation (e.g. verdict string value and its interaction with `certifiable`/signing and the completion_verdict schema's 'PASS or FAIL' verdict field) so every consumer maps it to the retryable-11/fail-closed contract.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the fetch=True freshness guarantee with ensure_fresh's throttle/best-effort semantics: state how the pin still reflects origin/tickets when reconverge is throttled or swallowed (e.g. bypass the throttle for gate pins, or fall back to resolving origin/tickets directly on the fetch=True path), and make the AC's 'contains everything origin/tickets holds' test exercise the throttled/failed-reconverge case.
evidence: Plan: 'first call the store's own reads.ensure_fresh(tracker) ... which fetches and reconverges ... THEN pin tracker HEAD. Because reconverge is merge-as-union, that HEAD is at least as fresh as origin/tickets'
reads.py:200-205,232-233 — ensure_fresh returns early when marker_age<60 (throttle) or _LOCAL_READ_CONTEXT/no_sync/sync-disabled
reads.py:252-255 — reconverge wrapped in try/except that swallows any failure (lock_timeout, network) so a stale HEAD is silently kept
Today's fetch=True path (repo_snapshot.py:568-571) resolves origin/tickets DIRECTLY via resolve_ref(fetch=True) — an unconditional fetch+pin of the remote ref, not subject to any per-minute throttle
findings.finding: For the fetch=True path, the plan's 'ensure_fresh THEN pin tracker HEAD' does not unconditionally match today's direct origin/tickets fetch-and-pin, because ensure_fresh is throttled (<=1/min) and best-effort (reconverge failures/lock-timeouts swallowed).
findings.location: Implementation plan step 1, fetch=True bullet; AC 'The fetch=True consumers ... still contains everything origin/tickets holds'
scenarios: A verify-completion/review-plan run within 60s of a prior read (throttle marker fresh) pins a tracker HEAD that has not fetched the latest origin/tickets
A concurrent background push holds the write lock; reconverge hits _RECONVERGE_LOCK_TIMEOUT, is swallowed, and HEAD lags origin/tickets
findings.suggested_fix: On the fetch=True path, either force an un-throttled reconverge before pinning (e.g. a gate-specific ensure_fresh call that ignores the <60s marker) or, when reconverge cannot confirm HEAD is at/ahead of origin/tickets, fall back to today's direct resolve_ref(f'{remote}/{ref}', fetch=True) pin — so the 'no content lost' invariant holds unconditionally, not just when the throttle window happens to be open.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define how the 'no verdict obtainable' state is represented in the completion_verdict contract: either a third admissible `verdict` enum value (and update the normalizing validators at contracts.py:138-145 and completion.py:454-455 to preserve it) or a distinct field, and specify how close_precheck's `verdict != "PASS"` branch maps it to the retryable exit.
evidence: Plan step 2: 'a non-PASS verdict carrying zero findings AND zero criteria is recorded as indeterminate rather than as a fabricated unmet criterion' and 'The verdict still blocks the close (fail-closed is preserved).'

completion_verdict contract validator hard-coerces the enum: `_norm_verdict` returns 'PASS' if input == 'PASS' else 'FAIL' (src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:138-145) — a third value like 'indeterminate' would be silently collapsed to FAIL before reconcile_verdict sees it.
reconcile_verdict repeats the same two-value coercion: `verdict = "PASS" if raw == "PASS" else "FAIL"` (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:454-455).

close_precheck branches solely on `verdict != "PASS"` (src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:543), so an indeterminate state must be carried in some field the exit-code logic can read — the plan does not name it.
findings.finding: Step 2 introduces an 'indeterminate' / 'no verdict obtainable' state for the completion_verdict LLM structured-output contract, but never defines its value vocabulary in the contract's `verdict` enum, which today admits exactly PASS/FAIL and is enforced by a normalizing validator that coerces any non-PASS value to FAIL.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; Acceptance Criteria line 'A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria is reported as "no verdict obtainable"'
scenarios: Executor adds an 'indeterminate' value to `verdict` and the existing normalizing validator collapses it to FAIL, silently defeating step 2.
Executor must decide between a new enum value vs a separate flag field but the plan gives no direction, risking an inconsistent contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Represent indeterminate as a distinct top-level field (e.g. `verdict_obtainable: false`) rather than a third verdict value, so the PASS/FAIL enum and its fail-safe validator stay intact; have close_precheck check that field before the `!= PASS` branch and route it to exit 11 with the distinct message.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-locate the wording fix: since the verifier prompt does not contain 'does not exist', specify the concrete edit site — add explicit prompt guidance instructing the model to phrase a not-found finding as 'not visible in the ticket snapshot I read' (rather than 'does not exist'), and identify whether COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE (completion.py:54-64) also needs the softened wording.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'The verifier prompt and the remediation guidance stop asserting a record does not exist and say "not visible in the ticket snapshot I read".'
search of src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md for 'does not exist' returns no matches; the string appears only in plan-review verifier prompts and unrelated modules (search_files results).
The framework-authored remediation guidance is COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE (src/rebar/llm/completion.py:54-64), which also does not contain 'does not exist'.
The 'confidently false no such comment exists' text is described in the plan's own Root cause 1b as model output, not prompt text.
findings.finding: Step 3 instructs to change 'the verifier prompt' to stop asserting a record 'does not exist', but the completion verifier prompt contains no such wording — the misleading 'does not exist' assertion is model-generated finding text, and the framework-authored remediation string is elsewhere — so the edit site named in the plan does not exist as described.
scenarios: Executor searches the verifier prompt for the 'does not exist' assertion to soften, finds nothing, and either edits the wrong file or omits the wording fix.

findings.finding: Step 2 introduces an 'indeterminate' / 'no verdict obtainable' state for completion verification but never defines how it is represented in the completion_verdict structured-output contract whose verdict vocabulary is exactly {PASS, FAIL} — and three separate points coerce/validate any non-PASS token back to FAIL.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 2; AC line 'A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria is reported as "no verdict obtainable"'
findings.suggested_fix: State whether indeterminacy is carried as a new field (e.g. `verdict=FAIL` plus a distinct `verdict_class='indeterminate'`/`no_verdict` marker, preserving the {PASS,FAIL} enum and fail-closed blocking) or a third verdict token; if the latter, enumerate the required updates to _norm_verdict, reconcile_verdict, _schema_verdict, and the completion_verifier/finalizer prompts so the token is not coerced away. close_precheck then reads that marker to choose exit 11 vs 1.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend Step 2's reconcile_verdict inventory to cover all three call sites (completion.py:513, gate_ops.py:297 completion_reconcile, completion_sidecar.py:323 build_payload), specifying how the new 'indeterminate' verdict flows through the workflow reconcile path and how build_payload records it (not as a FAIL sidecar).
evidence: Plan Step 2 names only 'close_precheck' as the consumer of the changed verdict.

src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:322-330 build_payload calls reconcile_verdict(v) then branches on str(v.get('verdict')).upper() == 'PASS' — a new non-PASS 'indeterminate' verdict falls through to the FAIL SCHEMA sidecar branch, mislabeling it as a failure record.

findings.finding: Step 2 changes reconcile_verdict's output (a non-PASS/empty-findings verdict becomes 'indeterminate' rather than a synthesized '(unspecified)' finding) but enumerates only close_precheck as the affected downstream consumer. reconcile_verdict has three structural call sites; two are omitted: gate_ops.completion_reconcile (src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py:297) and completion_sidecar.build_payload (src/rebar/llm/completion_sidecar.py:323).

findings.finding: Step 1 changes materialize_tickets to resolve the pin from the tracker-repo HEAD 'when that repo is present' for ALL callers, but review-plan already calls with fetch=True and currently pins origin/tickets; the plan does not confirm the new tracker-HEAD-first resolution leaves the fetch=True (review-plan) path behaving correctly, so a cross-consumer regression is neither ruled out nor covered by a criterion.
findings.location: Implementation plan step 1 vs Root cause 1 ('review-plan ... defaults to True')
findings.suggested_fix: Add a regression assertion covering the fetch=True caller and state in step 1 whether tracker-HEAD-first applies to fetch=True or only fetch=False.

findings.finding: Step 1 modifies the shared resolution logic of materialize_tickets for ALL callers, but only the close (fetch=False) path is analyzed; the review-plan/verify-completion caller that invokes it with fetch=True (via resolve_gate_handle in gate_source.py:115, reached from operations.py) is not enumerated as an affected consumer, even though the change re-bases the pin from the origin/tickets->local-branch chain onto tracker-repo HEAD.
findings.location: Implementation plan, step 1 ('Pin the ticket store at the LIVE store's own HEAD'); src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:568-576; src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:115

findings.finding: Fix 1 sources the pinned SHA from the separate .tickets-tracker repo's HEAD but does not specify which object store materialize_tickets reads that commit's tree from; the main repo's object DB (which _materialize_tree/_ensure_blobs_present operate against via root_dir) is ~6757 commits behind and may not contain the tracker-HEAD commit or its blobs, so materialization could fail with the very SHA the fix chooses.
findings.suggested_fix: State that when .tickets-tracker is present, both the SHA resolution AND the tree materialization (rev-parse, ls-tree, blob presence) run against the tracker repo's own object DB (git -C .tickets-tracker), reserving root_dir/origin only for the fallback chain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a criterion that the verifier's fenced ticket context and its show_ticket read return the same ticket view (the two gate halves agree) after the fix.
evidence: Root cause 1b: 'the two halves of the gate read different stores' and step 1 claims 'the two halves of the gate stop disagreeing'
AC3 verifies 'the pinned ticket snapshot reflects the live store at close time' but not that fenced-context and show_ticket agree
findings.finding: Root cause 1b (the fenced context reads the LIVE store while show_ticket reads the PINNED snapshot, so 'the two halves of the gate read different stores') is a distinct described defect, but no acceptance criterion directly asserts that after the fix the two halves return the SAME ticket view. AC3 asserts the pinned snapshot reflects live state, which is the mechanism, but does not verify the two halves now agree.
scenarios: A future change re-diverges the pin selection while the materialize_tickets test still passes, silently reintroducing the two-halves disagreement
findings.suggested_fix: Extend AC3 or add an AC: 'A regression test asserts the fenced <ticket_context> and the show_ticket tool return identical status/comments for a ticket at close time.'
